title: Replay chart-268 BIT repairs and prove their missing information
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Two literal changed-payload words send independent owner 679 through 785, 1584 and 1934, returning it in both native orientations. Restoring the two earliest old readers reduces forward errors from 104 to 89; each still fails 29 adjoint rows. Even granting identical free global broadcasts to every terminal with frozen histories, the exact minimum is three bits for the first word and two for the second. A separate fixed-clock Pro-derived proof closes a strictly larger 176-slot recoding family via an exact 32+30+2 partition and owner 221’s last chart-635 receipt at 19907.

## Task and overlap

Refined #7852 follow-up on main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, toolkit `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`, and native comparator #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Original one-deletion theorem #8000 `75d78d5877e522284197b782b1b8db237d18af58` and fixed-component restoration #8004 `fc26105676ad6d2afb59e39fed08f602b7ba0b66`. This supplement changes old payloads and distinguishes the 176-slot topology from the separately regraded side-readout word.

## Validation

Clean extraction checked both complete operators, both signed invoices, all 131,072 local assignments, 183 relaxed and 34 strict ingress tests, exact broadcast lower and upper controls, and the independent 176-slot derivation plus positive early-clock and corrupted native controls. The inner replay instructions are in README.md and AUDIT.md.

## Open next questions

The 176-slot case requires restoring the old chart-268 direction in time. Other retimings and joint changes to earlier paid values remain open. Both emitted modified words are diagnostic and qualify no new κ.
